findings.issue: The nine modality entries and the holdout test set were emitted as `resources` (range Dataset) in the core record but as `subsets` (range DataSubset) in the full record. In the full record the holdout entry carries `is_data_split: true`, a DataSubset-only slot; that flag is silently dropped in the core record, so the core record no longer states that the holdout set is a data split. The two records therefore assert different structural relationships for the same ten entities. If `subsets` exists on CoreDataset it should have been used; if it does not, the loss of `is_data_split` should have been carried in `notes` on the holdout entry rather than dropped.

Five of the six Creator objects carry no name in any declared field. `Creator` declares `principal_investigator`, `affiliations`, `credit_roles`, and `notes`; only the Rosenthal entry populates a naming field. For Bihorac, Jiang, Strekalova, Rashidi and Kwong the person's name appears only inside free-text `notes` ('Azra Bihorac, Bridge2AI CHoRUS leadership team.'), leaving the object structurally anonymous. This is the v3 failure mode: content parked in prose while declared fields stay empty.
Same defect as the full record: five of six Creator objects identify the person only in `notes`, with no declared naming field populated.

All five DistributionFormat objects populate only `notes`. The class declares `access_urls` and `notes`; the format information (OMOP, DICOM, WFDB, EDF+/Persyst, OHNLP tokens) is carried entirely as prose commentary rather than in any declared field, and the same content is already stated in `subsets` and `conforms_to_schema`. The bundle does supply access-route facts (cloud enclave, controlled access, registration + licensing agreement) that were placed in `license_and_use_terms` instead — correct per the v2 rule — leaving these objects with no declared content of their own.
Identical to the full record: five objects populating only `notes`, with no declared field carrying the format or access-URL information.

The single DistributionDate object populates only `notes` and its content explicitly states that the information the slot asks for is absent: 'Specific release dates are not stated in the source material.' Per the v2 rule, a value recording that the fact is unavailable has not answered the field; `release_dates` is empty and the slot should have been omitted.
Same defect as the full record: the object records the absence of release dates rather than supplying them, with `release_dates` unpopulated.

The second Instance object records the anticipated final dataset (100,000 admissions) as though it were a present instance population. The bundle presents this as a projection ('Anticipated Final Dataset'), not as instances the dataset contains. Composition slots describe what the dataset holds; the forward-looking figure is already correctly carried in `updates.update_details` and duplicating it as an Instance overstates current composition.
Same defect: the anticipated-final-dataset projection is emitted as a second Instance object rather than confined to `updates`.

Unreconciled internal inconsistency in the headline instance count. `instances[0].counts: 50000` is asserted as a scalar while the object's own `notes` records that the bundle carries two conflicting figures (50,000 admissions on chorus4ai.org versus 'over 45K unique admissions' as of August 2025 in the Cohort 2 webinar). The disagreement is disclosed in prose but a single figure is nonetheless asserted in the structured field, which is the silent selection the decision rules prohibit.

The single LabelingStrategy describes an annotation environment that is 'being developed' and states that labeling targets are not enumerated. No labeling has been documented as performed; the object records planned capability rather than an applied methodology. `data_annotation_platform` names an environment the bundle does not confirm exists in operational form.
Same defect as the full record: a prospective annotation capability recorded as an applied labeling strategy.

CTP-deid, privacy_scan_tool and DeGauss/UF-Geocoding are de-identification, privacy-scanning and geocoding utilities, not annotation tools. The bundle supports them as preprocessing tooling (already correctly recorded in `preprocessing_strategies`); only the OHNLP toolkit is plausibly an annotation tool. The slot's scope has been stretched to hold general tooling.
Same scope stretch: three of four listed tools are preprocessing/de-identification utilities rather than annotation tools.

The single Relationships object restates a coverage statistic already carried in `instances[0].notes` (7,642 admissions with radiology data) rather than describing a relationship between instances in the sense the slot declares (graph edges, ratings, links). Weakly supported as an instance-to-instance relationship.
The Splits object and the `subsets` holdout entry carry the same single fact about the sequestered holdout set, duplicating content across two Composition slots without adding structure.

Nine of the ten DataSubset entries carry synthetic fragment identifiers (e.g. `https://chorus4ai.org/#demographics`, `https://chorus4ai.org/#waveform-eeg`) that the bundle does not attest. The bundle names the modalities in a table but supplies no per-modality URLs or anchors. The `id` slot is required, so identifiers were necessary, but these are constructed rather than sourced.
Same constructed-identifier issue: ten fragment URIs under chorus4ai.org that the bundle does not attest.

The DataProtectionImpact object describes the project's general ethics and legal work rather than a conducted DPIA. The bundle documents an Ethics pillar, ethics focus groups, and legal-framework development, but never a data protection impact assessment. The content substantially duplicates `ethical_reviews[0].review_details`.
Same defect: general ethics-pillar activity recorded as a data protection impact assessment, duplicating `ethical_reviews`.

`reviewing_organization` is populated with 'CHoRUS consortium Ethics pillar (Ethical and Trustworthy AI)', which is a project workstream rather than a reviewing body. The bundle documents no IRB, ethics committee, or external review organization. The value gives the slot the shape of an ethics review without an attested reviewer.
Same: a project pillar named as the reviewing organization, with no IRB or ethics committee attested in the bundle.

Both Maintainer objects fold person names, institutional affiliations and email addresses into the single free-text `maintainer_details` string. `Maintainer` declares only `maintainer_details`, `role` and `notes`, so no better-fitting declared field exists, but the second entry additionally embeds curatorial attribution ('Contacts listed on the chorus-ai GitHub organization overview') in `notes`, mixing source commentary with contact content.

The dataset-level `notes` reproduces a source typo without flagging it as such in the address itself ('cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu'), and separately embeds an unresolved schema-attribution ambiguity about which OMOP data type carries the extensions. The disclosure is appropriate per the ambiguity rule, but the same misspelled address is repeated verbatim in `maintainers[0].maintainer_details` without the '(address as printed in the source)' qualifier, so the qualifier does not travel with the value.

Same: misspelled email reproduced in both `notes` (qualified) and `maintainers[0].maintainer_details` (unqualified). The core `notes` additionally absorbs the holdout-test-set fact displaced by the `subsets`→`resources` substitution, which is a reasonable mitigation but leaves a composition fact in dataset-level prose.

`status` is a free-text summary of release maturity. The bundle carries a more specific and directly quotable status signal — the website banner 'This repoitory is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives' — which was placed in `notes` and `regulatory_restrictions.notes` instead. Not incorrect, but the slot's value is inferred synthesis rather than an attested status string.

Omission the bundle arguably supports: the Cohort 2 webinar lists 'Working command of English' as a required applicant skill and all documented materials are English. Weak evidence for the dataset's own content language, so omission is defensible, but it was not considered.

Omission. The bundle supplies the NIH award attribution sentence and award number OT2OD032701 that the project website directs users to acknowledge. This is an acknowledgement requirement rather than a citation format, so omission is defensible; noted as a borderline supported omission.

Omission. The bundle states '23 Tb Waveform data' for the current release. This covers one modality only and the unit notation is ambiguous (Tb vs TB), so omitting the dataset-level total is correct; the figure is preserved in the waveform subset `notes`. Recorded as a considered omission rather than a defect.

All five ExternalResource objects use `external_resources` (the URL) plus `notes`. The class declares `archival`, `future_guarantees` and `restrictions`, none populated. The bundle does not attest archival status or future guarantees for these links, so omission of those fields is correct; flagged only to record that the objects are minimally populated by evidence limits rather than by oversight.

Substantial content overlap across the four Motivation/Uses slots: the holdout-set-for-external-validation fact appears in `purposes[2]`, `tasks[3]`, `intended_uses[1]` and `future_use_impacts[0]`; the training/education fact appears in `purposes[4]`, `intended_uses[2]` and `existing_uses`. Each placement is individually defensible against its slot description, but the repetition inflates apparent coverage.

summary: Both records are well grounded in the declared bundle — no fabricated facts, no external-knowledge leakage, no prior-D4D reuse, and the two genuine source conflicts (50,000 vs 45K admissions; the ambiguous OMOP-extension row) are surfaced rather than hidden. Enum usage is valid throughout (credit_roles, bias_type, limitation_type, role, confidentiality_level all draw on defined values) and all required keys are present (Dataset.id, DataSubset.id, RawDataSource.source_description). The dominant defect is structural rather than factual: five of six Creator objects in each record are anonymous, carrying the person's name only in free-text `notes` while the declared naming fields stay empty — precisely the v3 failure mode. Second, the core record substitutes `resources` (range Dataset) for the full record's `subsets` (range DataSubset), silently dropping the `is_data_split: true` flag on the holdout test set and leaving the paired records asserting different structure for the same ten modality entities. Third, several objects are shaped but hollow: all five DistributionFormat entries and the single DistributionDate entry populate only `notes`, with the DistributionDate value explicitly recording that release dates are unavailable — an omission dressed as an answer. Lower-severity issues cluster around slot-scope stretch (preprocessing utilities filed as machine_annotation_tools; the Ethics pillar named as a reviewing_organization; general ethics work recorded as a DPIA), forward-looking content placed in composition slots (the 100,000-admission projection as an Instance; a not-yet-built annotation environment as a labeling_strategy), constructed subset identifiers the bundle does not attest, and redundancy across the Motivation/Uses slots. Recommended remediation before Phase 4: populate Creator naming fields for all six creators; reconcile the subsets/resources divergence and preserve the holdout split flag; drop distribution_dates and either drop distribution_formats or move its content to a field that carries it; demote the anticipated-final-dataset Instance to updates only; and either surface both admission counts structurally or qualify the asserted 50000.
